thought.text: Web docker service lacks `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`. The guide's primary frontend path is `npm run dev` in the tooling container on port 3000. Let me set that up.

The web_application docker image is built without .env.local, so NEXTAUTH_SECRET is missing. The guide's web frontend setup says to use `npm run dev` for the tooling path, but the docker build path (port 3003) needs an env file. The guide's docker path (`web_application` service on 3003) doesn't mention env setup. This is a documented-insufficient area, but I can fix it by supplying env at runtime.

Actually the primary documented path for the web frontend is the tooling container `npm run dev` on port 3000. Let me follow that path. But also, the built docker image could work if env vars are provided. Since the guide says to test the frontend build with baseUrl http://web_application:3000, the docker path is a supported method.

Let me set up the web_application in the tooling container as the guide documents (the primary method). First cp .env.local.example .env.local and add the token, then npm ci and npm run dev.

But let me also consider: the web_application docker service needs env. I could supply an env_file. Actually the compose service has no env_file. Let me fix the docker path too by adding environment variables. But primary guide path is npm run dev in tooling.

Let me do the tooling path first.

Also note API_DOMAIN=http://api in .env.local.example — from tooling container, `api` resolves. Good.

Let me set up web frontend in tooling.

action.command: cd /workspace && docker compose exec -T tooling bash -lc 'cd web_application && cp -n .env.local.example .env.local && grep -q "^API_BEARER_TOKEN=." .env.local && echo "token present" || sed -i "s#^API_BEARER_TOKEN=.*#API_BEARER_TOKEN=1|WEhI5anY6yAh3oK5kT9UANurD18WxMzXmbZrRQyt6236cae3#" .env.local; grep -E "API_BEARER_TOKEN|API_DOMAIN|NEXTAUTH" .env.local' 2>&1 | grep -v level=warning
